answer: Attention-escrow admission. Each identity must hold a live kernel of unanswered inbound queries: it earns the right to act only while its oldest pending request stays under a short age cap, checked every round. A grove of identities therefore demands parallel, sustained human response capacity, not one-time setup. An attacker running N sybils pays N concurrent attention streams and loses each identity the moment any queue goes stale. The oasis of usable identities stays small because idle capacity cannot be banked or transferred between them.
